speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. As Dr. Agent, I will ask you questions to understand your condition. How long have you been experiencing symptoms, and what specific signs have you noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, has the newborn exhibited any signs of jaundice, fever, poor feeding, or respiratory distress in the first 24 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a continuous heart murmur, bluish macules that do not blanch, and cloudy lenses is highly suggestive of a specific congenital syndrome. Given the history of no prenatal care, has the newborn's mother experienced a mumps infection during her first trimester of pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Newborn, no past medical history available. Social history: Mother is a primigravida, no prenatal care received.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rubella Congenital Syndrome (German Measles). The combination of a continuous heart murmur (PDA), bluish non-blanching macules (petechiae/purpura), and cloudy lenses (cataracts) constitutes the classic triad of congenital rubella, confirmed by the history of maternal mumps-like infection and lack of prenatal immunization.
